_comment: Changes to the 1.02 eboot's code, applied by the recompiler (third_party/recomp/recomp/recompile.py --overrides; game.json recomp_overrides). The game's bytes stay as they are; the JIT runs the original code. docs/decisions.md D16, docs/01-research.md 'Mouse camera'.
prelude: // The mouse camera (utakata D16). shinobido2.exe keeps the mouse's running totals in the page left over
// after the eboot's data (0x819f6d14-0x819f7000, which the game never uses): +0 'UTMC' while it drives
// the camera, +4 yaw (right) and +8 pitch (down), in 1/1024 of a degree. +12 counts the calls below, so
// it can tell whether a camera that takes the mouse is running. Each place that turns the camera by the
// right stick (the field camera, the hook's aim, ...) adds what the mouse moved since its own last call
// to that frame's turn, before the game's own limits, as it takes the stick on its own. A place not
// called for a moment (another camera, a menu, a scene) drops what moved meanwhile.
// milliseconds of a monotonic clock, from the system C library: a module built for Android can't
// use libc++'s clock (the front end doesn't export it, so the module wouldn't load)
// radians to add to this frame's turn at `site` (0-7) along `axis` (0 yaw, right; 1 pitch, down)
inline float ut_mouse_turn(int site, int axis) {
const bool fresh = ut_mouse_at[site] != 0 && now - ut_mouse_at[site] < 150u;
const float degrees = std::fmax(-90.0f, std::fmin(90.0f, static_cast<float>(moved) / 1024.0f));

overrides.why: field camera (0x810074d6): this frame's yaw (radians, negative turns right), plus the mouse's
field camera (0x810074d6): this frame's pitch (radians, positive looks down), plus the mouse's
the hook's aim (0x81007406, called by 0x8100cce6): this frame's yaw, plus the mouse's
the hook's aim (0x81007342, called by 0x8100cce6): this frame's pitch, plus the mouse's
camera mode 0x8100b86e (the field camera's twin): this frame's yaw, plus the mouse's
camera mode 0x8100b86e: this frame's pitch, plus the mouse's
